rv.q: This production delivers the full "Strange Loop" monty by foregrounding what Chicago theater does best.
There’s truly no other show like A Strange Loop.
An ambitious task, but “A Strange Loop” succeeds in it, creating something wholly individual.
“A Strange Loop” is a masterpiece, and Jackson is well-deserving of the 2020. Pulitzer Prize.
It is, in short, theatre at its finest.
More than anything else, what impressed me about the show was its willingness to push itself and its audience into darker, uncharted territory.
This new musical is another dazzling and emotional ride, a very different, unconventional kind of show that’s also so electrifying that it will haunt your mind and burrow into your soul.
Jackson’s story resists earnestness while also celebrating it, which is pretty much my favorite blend in musicals.
As in love with the show as I was in 2022, my care for it shines even brighter because of the Raven and About Face co-production.
"A Strange Loop" is the best kind of new musical—in that it’s hard to explain.
And exuberant/painful truth telling is exactly what makes A Strange Loop such an insightful and compelling contemporary musical.
Michael R. Jackson's A Strange Loop is a phenomenal, well-written musical.

The cast is a treat. Although all different heights and sizes, they work and move well together, and their boisterous voices blend beautifully in these all-too-familiar theater stories, albeit a little NYC-centric.
A Strange Loop is bold, blunt and brilliant!
And let’s not forget that this is crafted as a musical- it’s vastly entertaining, filled with big, clear voices and wickedly funny.

cn.t: Critics hail this Pulitzer and Tony-winning musical as bold, brilliant, and essential—a fearless, meta exploration of a Black queer artist's psyche that's inventive, deeply human, and among the most important American musicals of the past decade.
